title: Heat Pump in -30 C. Canadian Winter Struggles
summary: A Canadian podcaster reports his second winter with an air-source heat pump with resistance backup, including efficiency loss near -30°C and outdoor unit icing.

assertions.quote: as they get to that minus 30 they're essentially working they lose their efficiency
when it's down at minus 30 you're essentially it's the same efficiency as a sort of an old-fashioned electric heater
there's some now that work down to minus 30
there's a backup resistive heater which is essentially a 10,000 watt heater simple mechanism not efficient
this is the second winter that I've had it and it's basically worked
the fan stopped spinning because there was just a little bit too much ice in there

verdicts.note: Blocked coils or frozen fans cut output; manufacturers recommend raised mounts and clearance in snowy areas.

In the snowy 2015 winter several outdoor units were encased in snow or ice and, without clearance, 'could not provide heating'; buried units for up to a month also visibly lowered that winter's measured efficiencies.
